sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

content.text:
Case V16: segment the vascular soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 91x91x51 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case V16 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(91, 91, 51) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: vascular soft-tissue tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 25/51 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.text: axial 20/51 | crop mask | marks edges | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 5/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking more closely, the mask in axial 20 covers the upper-right bright region but misses the lower-left posterior-lateral bright area, roughly x 260-390, y 380-500 in the clean crop. The lesion seems to extend further laterally, with bright tissue from y 270 to 500 on the patient's right side, and the mask misses the lateral portion around x 260-300, y 280-480, plus the lower part near y 430-500. I'm trying to figure out whether that lateral bright region is actually part of the lesion or something else.

I'm thinking the lesion looks like a heterogeneous bright mass with a dark center, possibly a vessel, and the lateral bright band might belong to it. I'm considering adding a positive point near the lower-left bright area, checking edge marks like E6, E2, E14, and E7 to see which fall inside versus outside the current mask, but since the current view only shows edge marks, I need to pick from what's visible. Rather than guessing coordinates, I think calling seg_candidates would be more useful to get better suggestions.

C1 seems to be the larger candidate region, extending into surrounding bright areas laterally and posteriorly, possibly including a vessel-like band, though it's hard to tell if that's part of the tumor or just adjacent vasculature. I want to examine axial slice 20 more closely, where the lesion shows a bright region with a dark center.

I should also check whether the lateral bright strip and the curved anterior band are actually fascia or vessels separate from the lesion itself. I think I'll try refining the segmentation with a positive point on the lower-left bright region, and then switch to a coronal view through the lesion's centroid to better understand its full extent.

Now I'm shifting to check the axial view, where it looks like the mask is missing the lateral bright strip, so I want to examine specific axial slices more closely.

content.text: axial 14/51 | crop mask | marks edges | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 8/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
At axial slice 14, I'm checking the lesion boundaries against the mask coverage — the bright region spans roughly x 290-500, y 280-500, and the mask after offset correction covers x 282-492, which mostly aligns but the upper-left bright lobe around x 300-360, y 290-330 appears to extend slightly outside the mask's top edge.

I'm also noticing a bright lateral band running from y 130 to 560 along the lateral wall, which could be a vessel or fascial structure rather than tumor tissue, so I shouldn't include it as lesion without more certainty. For the missing upper lobe coverage, I'm considering adding a positive scribble or point near clean coordinates (330, 310), but none of my existing marks land exactly there — I may need to use a finer annotation tool or just accept an existing candidate mask like C1 to extend coverage.

Rather than guessing blindly, I'll get a zoomed view with fine marks around E10 and E6 so I can place a precise positive point on the upper-left bright lobe at axial 14 and check whether that lateral strip is truly separate from the main tumor blob or connects to it at other slices.

content.text: axial 14/51 | crop marks | marks fine | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 9/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking at the crop coordinates, the mask seems to roughly align with the bright lesion area in this slice, though there's a lateral band near the edge that may need checking against the mask boundary.

I'm uncertain whether that lateral bright band is part of the actual lesion or a separate structure like a vessel or fascia, so I should check the adjacent slices to see how the mask treats this region there.

content.text: axial 25/51 | crop mask | marks edges | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 10/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
The axial 25 mask lines up well with the lesion's bright region, so I move on to checking axial 30 and 33 for the lower extent and axial 10 for the upper extent.

Looking further, I notice smaller lesion areas appearing in axial 5 and 9 too, with the overall mask spanning axial 3 to 41. I need to verify whether the mask actually covers this upper range by checking axial 8 directly.

content.text: axial 8/51 | crop mask | marks edges | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 11/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking at axial slice 8, I'm noting the ring-like bright lesion with a dark center, and the mask appears to only partially cover the lesion—missing parts of the bright area around the rim.

There's also a lateral bright band running from anterior toward the mass, which could be an extension of the lesion along fascia, or could just be a vessel or subcutaneous structure—I need to think more about the anatomy here before deciding how to handle it.

This looks like a small cross-section, maybe a limb, with a fat-suppressed T2 sequence where fluid is bright and fat is dark. Given the uncertainty around the lateral band, I think the safest approach is to keep the mask focused on the core bright blob and its rim, since the existing mask already looks reasonable at the key slices.

I'm checking slice 8, where the mask is patchy, and considering whether to add positive points on the bright ring rather than trying to trace a full polygon around the lesion at every level, which would be too laborious. Comparing the bright ring regions to the current mask coverage, it seems like most of the ring—upper, lower, and left portions—is already reasonably captured, so the mask is fairly close to correct overall.

The bigger question is the dark central region within the ring, which could be a flow void or necrosis in a vascular lesion versus a separate structure like a vessel or nerve. Since this dark round area with its bright rim appears consistently at the medial-posterior edge across slices 14 and 20, it looks more like a distinct anatomical structure than part of the lesion itself, so I'm leaning toward excluding it from the mask.

The lateral band is trickier — it's continuous with the lesion in axial 14 but looks like a separate linear structure, possibly fascia or a vessel, so I'd mostly exclude it even though candidate C1 includes it. I'm thinking the best path forward is to keep the current mask with some refinement in the upper slices, checking slices 3-8 to see where the mask actually starts, and considering whether additional seed points would help the model grow the segmentation correctly without leaking into that lateral band. I also want to cross-check against the coronal and sagittal views to confirm whether the mask covers the whole lesion.

Looking at the dimensions more carefully, the lesion appears to span roughly 14×17×30mm given the j-extent (36-53), i-extent (54-68), and k-extent (3-41), putting the volume around 4-5 mL — consistent with my earlier estimate. The axial sheet confirms faint remnants of the lesion persist through slice 38 and fade by 41, so the lower boundary of the mask seems about right. Now I want to check the sagittal view at slice 61 with the mask overlaid to verify the upper and lower extents are captured correctly.

content.text: sagittal 61/91 | crop mask | marks edges | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 12/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Checking the sagittal 61 slice, the lesion is oval-shaped and the mask fits reasonably well, though I need to verify how the mask's lower tail and anterior boundary line up against the actual lesion edges, accounting for the panel offset.

Converting to clean coordinates confirms the mask's left and posterior boundaries match the lesion edges well, and the top boundary also aligns. The vertical bright band nearby looks like a separate vessel/fascia structure that's correctly excluded from the mask, and the dark center region is properly enclosed within the mask boundary.

I'm leaning toward rejecting candidate C1 since it touches the mask and picks up the lateral band, while C2/C3 look like separate vessel structures not adjacent to the lesion. The mask seems reasonable overall, though I'm considering whether a fill-holes refinement might help with dark centers seen in some axial slices.

Checking whether the dark center hole in axial slice 20 got filled by the mask — it looks like it did. Now I want to verify the lower portion of the mask captures the lesion remnant visible around axial slices 30-38, so I'll pull up axial slice 35 with the mask overlay to confirm the boundary extends far enough to include that bright region.

content.text: axial 33/51 | crop mask | marks edges | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 13/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: At axial slice 33, the mask aligns well with the bright lesion region. I should also check the upper extent around slices 3-8, particularly slice 8 where the ring structure appeared only partially covered, so let me examine slice 5 with the mask overlay next.

content.text: axial 5/51 | crop mask | marks edges | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 14/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
At axial 5, I'm tracing that same thin bright band as it curves down around a dark circular structure, trying to confirm it's the upper extension of the lesion along the lateral wall.

Given the ring pattern seen at axial 8 (bright rim surrounding a dark center at roughly x400,y450, with bright tissue above, left, below, and right), I think this dark circle is likely a vessel encased by tumor tissue, and the axial 5 band is consistent with that same wrap-around pattern — I'll keep the current mask without further smoothing since fragmenting it more wouldn't clarify anything.

The dark core persists at axial 14 and 20, positioned adjacent to the bright lesion rather than inside it, which makes me think it's a separate vascular structure (flow void) rather than necrotic tumor core — I'll leave it excluded from the mask since the inclusion rule is about rims around bright cores, not dark ones. I'm fairly confident in the current segmentation and don't think refinement is needed; I'll move to finishing the review and checking a coronal slice to confirm no lateral bright tissue was missed before finalizing.

arguments.reason: Single component ~4-5 mL covering the bright heterogeneous lobulated mass on the patient-right side; outline matches the lesion in axial 14/20/25/33 and sagittal 61. Uncertainty: the thin lateral bright band along the wall and the dark round structure at the posterior-medial edge were excluded as likely vessel/fascia; upper tip (axial 3-8) is patchy.

content.text:
Final review of v1: volume 4.0 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 3–41, coronal 36–53, sagittal 54–68 | tool calls 15/40, prompts 1/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates (second image): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong).
C1 add 11 mL, touches mask on its right, left and posterior sides, level with the mask
C2 add 5.8 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly posterior of the mask
C3 add 5.4 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly anterior of the mask
C4 add 3.5 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly left of the mask
C5 add 3.0 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly anterior of the mask
candidate image: one row per candidate, columns axial / coronal / sagittal through the candidate (green outline = current mask, magenta outline + light tint = candidate; judge the tissue inside the magenta outline). For each candidate decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept) or normal tissue (reject). Accept with seg_accept and call seg_finish again for a new review; if none belong, confirm with the review code. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "2263" to save it.

content.text: case V16 finished (confidence medium); final mask saved from v1 | final volume 4.0 mL, components 1 (largest 100.0%) | tool calls 16/40, prompts 1/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

The segmentation for case V16 is saved as a single component of about 4.0 mL, with medium confidence.

I used one positive point prompt on the bright, lobulated mass on the patient's right side, then checked the outline in axial, coronal and sagittal views. It fits the lesion well at the middle and lower slices (axial 14, 20, 25, 33 and sagittal 61). The final review showed no lesion tissue beyond either end of the mask.

Three areas are the uncertain parts:
- **Lateral wall band:** a thin bright band along the lateral wall, which connects to the lesion, was left out. I judged it to be a vessel or fascia.
- **Dark round structure:** a dark round structure with a bright rim on the posterior-medial edge was also left out, as a likely vessel.
- **Upper tip:** the mask near axial slices 5–8 is patchy, because the lesion there is a thin ring-like structure.

I rejected all five automatic candidates. C1 (11 mL) took in the lateral band and surrounding tissue, and C2–C5 lie outside the lesion.

Tool use was 16 of 40 calls and 1 of 15 model prompts.
